SUBJECT:  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION R10-27 UNILATERALLY RESOLVING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2010-2011 MEET AND CONFER
  IMPASSE BETWEEN THE CITY AND THE PALOS VERDES ESTATES
  POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION

DATE:  NOVEMBER 9, 2010

ISSUE

Shall the City adopt Resolution R10-27 unilaterally resolving the Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Meet and
Confer Impasse between the City and the Palos Verdes Estates Police Officers’ Association?

BACKGROUND AND ANALYSIS

Resolution R09-26, resolving an impasse between the City and the Palos Verdes Estates’ Police
Officers’ Association for Fiscal Year 2009-2010, expired June 30, 2010. Therefore, in recent
weeks, the City has been engaged in labor negotiations with the Palos Verdes Estates Police
Officers’ Association (POA) representatives. Pursuant to Government Code sections 3500 through
3511, the City has engaged in good faith negotiations with the POA regarding proposed changes to
wages, hours and other terms and conditions of employment for Fiscal Year 2010- 2011.

The City received the POA’s first proposal on August 26, 2010. Subsequently, the City and POA
met on September 20, 2010, and exchanged additional proposals. Thereafter, the City and POA met
again on September 30, 2010, and exchanged further proposals.

Subsequently, on October 8, 2010, in a letter to the POA’s attorney, Rob Wexler, the City
communicated that the City offer presented on September 30, 2010 was the City’s Last, Best and
Final offer. The POA did not respond, and on October 19, 2010, in a separate letter to the POA, the
City declared an impasse. The POA subsequently notified the City that its membership would vote
on the City’s Last, Best, and Final offer. This vote resulted in the POA rejecting the City’s Last,
Best, and Final offer. Therefore, the City reaffirms that the parties are at impasse and have not
reached an agreement for Fiscal Year 2010-2011.

To resolve the impasse between the City and the POA, staff recommends that the City Council
unilaterally impose its Last, Best and Final offer. This would ensure prompt resolution and still
provide a benefit to POA members. The POA has been informed that staff would forward this
recommendation to Council at its November 9, 2010 open meeting.

 The City’s Last, Best and Final offer (as seen attached) includes the following provisions:

  1) Term: One Year – July 1, 2010 to June 30, 2011.

  2) On November 12, 2010 (date modified), a one-time stipend in the amount of $500 will be
  paid to full-time members of the unit.

  3) The City’s contribution toward health insurance will be increased from $1,030 to $1,105 per
  month effective July 1, 2010.

  4) Effective November 8, 2010, Special Assignment Pay (motorcycle, detective, and canine
  patrol) will increase from 4% to 5%.

ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO COUNCIL

  1. The City Council may choose to adopt Resolution R10-27.
  2. The City Council may choose not to adopt Resolution R10-27.
  3. The City Council may postpone adoption of Resolution R10-27.

CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R10-27 unilaterally resolving the Fiscal
Year 2010-2011 Meet and Confer Impasse between the City and the Palos Verdes Estates Police
Officers’ Association.

BUDGET IMPACT

The cost of unilaterally imposing the City’s Last, Best and Final offer is $30,772, which represents
0.9% increase in pay for employees in this unit.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION R10-26; AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF
  OBSOLETE RECORDS OF THE CITY MANAGER, CITY CLERK,
  TREASURER, FINANCE AND PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENTS

The Issue

Shall the City Council adopt Resolution R10-26, which authorizes destruction of specific obsolete
records of the City Manager, City Clerk, Treasurer, Finance and Public Works Departments?

Analysis and Findings

The City has a formal records management program which allows for the orderly transfer,
maintenance and/or destruction of City records. The retention period for specific records is outlined
in the policy in accordance with state regulations and City policy. With storage space at a premium,
it is important for the staff to keep current with the records program.

The City Attorney has reviewed and approved the request for destruction as being in conformance
with the City’s records management program and retention schedule.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

1.  Adopt Resolution R10-26.

2.  Decline to adopt the Resolution.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R10-26; authorizing the destruction of
specific obsolete records of the City Manager, City Clerk, Treasurer, Finance and Public Works
Departments.

FROM:  JUDY SMITH, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  PALOS VERDES TENNIS CLUB FY 2011 OPERATING
  AND CAPITAL BUDGETS

The Issue

Shall the City Council review and approve the FY 2011 Palos Verdes Tennis Club (PVTC)
operating and capital budgets?

Analysis and Findings

The Palos Verdes Tennis Club fiscal year begins on January 1 and the concession agreement
requires that the Club submit their budget to the City for review. The PVTC Board of Directors
approved the 2011 budgets at its October meeting. On October 25th, Council liaisons Bird and
Goodhart met with Club President Dave Kleinman, Treasurer Bruce Merchant and Manager John
Hall to review the budget.

2010 Projected Results: The 2010 adopted budget assumed net income of $4,960 on revenues of
$555,450 and expenses of $550,490. The 2010 budget was based on 390 members. Based on actual
performance through September 30th, the Club now projects net income of approximately $700 on
revenue of $507,000 and expenses of $506,300. Actual results for FY 2009 showed an operating
loss of ~$5,000. As in past years, most of the lower actual to budget performance is related to
program and lesson revenues, which are in turn offset by lower costs for these functions.

2011 Operating Budget: The 2011 operating budget is based on an assumption of 387 members,
which is the current membership. The budget reflects estimated net income of $670 on revenue of
$510,130 and expenses of $509,460. Both revenues and expenditures reflect a 0.6% increase
compared to projected 2010 yearend. No dues increase is proposed. Monthly resident dues are $65
and non-resident dues are $80. Dues were last increased in 2006 (+$10/month). In the 2011 budget,
dues ($320,220) and guest fees ($10,500) represent 65% of total operating revenue.

The challenge for the Club in this budget, as the past several years, will be meeting the slim
operating margin. The Club believes its healthy cash balance of $345,420 (including capital funds
of $82,375), equal to 65% of the proposed operating budget, is more than sufficient to cover a
minor operating shortfall, should one occur. Furthermore, given the difficult economy, the Club
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
NOVEMBER 9, 2010
  8
 believes a dues increase at this time would further exacerbate the budget due to an expected drop in
membership that would occur as a result of an increase.

2011 Capital Budget: The Club anticipates a beginning capital balance of $50,200 (excluding a
$40,000 reserve for Clubhouse roof replacement). The proposed capital budget assumes income
(initiation fees) of $30,000 and expenditures of $56,600 for an ending balance (12-30-11) of
$23,600. Expenditures include court resurfacing (3 courts), at a cost of $21,600, which includes
hydro-blasting. This is a more expensive process than normal resurfacing and involves a high
pressure water treatment to remove previous paint layers in order to get down to slab, before
applying a new court surface.

The budget also calls for fence painting ($19,500) and windscreen replacements ($15,500). In order
to paint the fence, windscreens must be removed and since much of the cost of windscreens is
installation, the projects should be undertaken at the same time. The Club did indicate, it will
carefully review its capital fund position in the late spring and determine at that point whether to
proceed with these items or wait until FY 2012. The only capital item anticipated at this time for
FY 2012 is court resurfacing (2 courts requiring hydro-blast treatment) at a cost $13,600.

The City Council liaisons will report on their meeting, which included discussions related to new
member recruitment. There is currently no waiting list for Club membership and the Club offers an
installment plan for payment of the initiation fee that make membership easily affordable.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

  1. Approve the FY 2011 Palos Verdes Tennis Club operating and capital budgets.

  2. Decline to approve the FY 2011 operating and capital budgets. This would require the Club
  and Board of Directors to change the budgets to address City Council concerns.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the FY 2011 Palos Verdes Tennis Club operating
and capital budgets.

Budget Impact

The PVTC is a non-profit entity whose budget is separate from the City’s. The PVTC pays a 10%
concession fee on gross revenues (dues, guest fees, and food and beverage sales) to the City. The
Club’s FY 2011 budget includes a cost of $33,250 for payment of these fees to the City.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
NOVEMBER 9, 2010

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 6:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Humphrey.

  City Treasurer Sherwood, Administrative Analyst Davis,

PALOS VERDES ESTATES POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION

Councilmember Bird was in favor of the resolution and commented that he believes the PVE police
officers are doing an outstanding job for the City and citizens. He wished that the economy was
such that the Council could offer raises. He commended the police department personnel for the
manner in which they approached the negotiations which speaks to their professionalism. The
citizens appreciate the job that they are doing.

Mayor Humphrey said Councilmember Bird spoke for the entire Council.

It was moved by Councilmember Bird, seconded by Councilmember Perkins, and unanimously
approved to adopt Resolution R10-27 unilaterally resolving the FY2010-11 Meet and Confer
Impasse between the City and the Palos Verdes Estates Police Officers’ Association.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC - none

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NEW BUSINESS

PALOS VERDES TENNIS CLUB FY2011 OPERATING AND CAPITAL BUDGETS

Assistant City Manager Smith reported that the Palos Verdes Tennis Club fiscal year begins on January
1st. The Board of Directors of the Club approved the budget at their October meeting and on October
25th Council Liaisons Bird and Goodhart met with Club representatives. The 2011 Operating Budget
assumes membership of 387. The concession agreement allows maximum membership of 480 and
when the membership drops below 400 active members the Club is allowed to admit non-residents
with a maximum of 120 non-resident members. As of September 30th there were 295 active PVE
resident members and 92 non-resident members. The 2011 budget estimates net income of $670 with
revenues of $510,000 and expenses of $509,460. The budget does not include a dues increase. The
Club does have a healthy cash balance of over $300,000. Given the difficult economy, the Club is
reluctant to raise dues. For the Capital Budget, the Club anticipates a beginning balance of $50,200
CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 9, 2010  2
 which excludes a reserve of $40,000 that is set aside for a clubhouse roof replacement. The proposed
Capital Budget assumes income of $30,000 and expenditures of $56,600 for an ending balance of
$23,600. The expenditures proposed for next year include court resurfacing, fence painting, and wind
screen replacement. Manager Smith said there was extensive discussion related to new member
recruitment at the Liaison meeting.

Tennis Club Manager John Hall gave a brief review of the amenities available at the Tennis Club
including 12 courts, 10 of which are lit. There is a very active women’s league, men’s night tennis, a
junior program, social events, a Pro Shop, a beautiful clubhouse, and newly remodeled locker rooms.
The cost to join is a $2,000 initiation fee and a $65 per month dues payment. He offered free lessons to
any resident interested in becoming a member. The Club has six certified tennis pros available for
lessons.

Councilmember Goodhart complimented John Hall for his management of the Club. He said the
facility is very unique and the maintenance is top-notch even during tough economic times. He said
much time was spent during the Liaison meeting evaluating the various options the Directors
implemented to recruit members, minimize costs and to provide an attractive environment for tennis
players. He commended the Club for their efforts during these tough times.

Councilmember Perkins asked what sort of marketing the Club was doing. Mr. Hall said he sends
welcome letters to new residents with gift certificates enclosed, he advertises through the Backpack
flyer program (schools), and the City Newsletter. Councilmember Perkins suggested an Open House
as that approach was successful for the PV Stables. She is concerned with the declining membership
numbers and marketing is important. Mr. Hall said the Yonex tournaments attract new people to the
Club.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked if Mr. Hall had contacted Terrenea resort for possible play from their resort
guests. Mr. Hall had contacted Terrenea last year, but they have a contract with another Club that is
closer and PV courts are usually full in the mornings when resort guests would likely want to play.
Mayor Pro Tem Rea congratulated Mr. Hall on a great job and his frugal management style.

It was moved by Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Bird and unanimously
approved to approve the FY2011 Palos Verdes Tennis Club operating and capital budgets.

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS’ REPORTS

Councilmember Goodhart reported his attendance at the Educator of the Year award dinner sponsored
by the Peninsula Rotary, the Neighborhood Watch Annual Meeting and the Breakfast Club meeting
where Chief Dreiling gave a speech on honor.

Councilmember Perkins reported on the SBCCOG meeting where the speaker was Paul Herzog from
the Surfrider Foundation who discussed the Ocean Friendly Gardens program.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea reported that the CJPIA resource center will be going on-line so City staff will be
able access the entire resource library of the CJPIA including webinars.

Councilmember Bird congratulated the Norris Center for the Performing Arts for their Rising Stars
Program which benefits foster children. He reported that Palos Verdes High School won their first
round of the Constitutional Rights Foundation Mock Trial Competition.

Mayor Humphrey said she also attended the Educator of the Year award dinner along with City
Manager Hoefgen. She, Manager Hoefgen and Councilmember Goodhart also attended the League of
California Cities Legislative Delegation event.

ADJOURNMENT
